From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP + perf eval: need test access and a results summary for exec review

Hi Emily —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a first-draft MAP (DataWave_MAP_v1.xlsx) and below is a short perf evaluation plan plus an executive-friendly summary of preliminary results from our staging runs.

MAP highlights (milestones and owners):
- 2026-06-12: Test credentials & ephemeral env details provided by Redwood (owner: Monica).
- 2026-06-14 to 2026-06-16: Evaluation window (owner: DataWave engineering) — load windows within agreed times (see schedule).
- 2026-06-17: Redwood delivers consolidated perf report and recommendations (owner: Laura).
- 2026-06-21: Procurement completes initial review / pricing confirmation (owner: DataWave procurement).
- 2026-06-30: Target close / contract signature (owners: both teams).

Evaluation plan (short):
- Models & endpoint: rw-infer/gptx-small-13b (quantized variant) on c5-like inference pool. Endpoint: https://staging.redwood.com/dw-test/api
- Measurement surface: P50/P95 request latency (ms), TTFT (ms), sustained throughput (req/s), aggregate tokens/sec, and behavior under increasing concurrency (1, 4, 8, 16 concurrent connections).
- Workload: 200 unique prompts representative of your 75-token avg output; mixed prompt lengths (short/medium/long).
- Acceptance targets (suggested): P95 < 550ms; TTFT < 120ms; throughput >= 300 req/s at 8 concurrent connections with 95% success rate.

Logistics: access & keys
- Test account: created (DataWave-staging@redwood.com).
- API key (ephemeral): DATAWAVE_TEST_KEY=dw-stg-9XkL (valid until 2026-06-18). DO NOT use in production.
- Test endpoint: https://staging.redwood.com/dw-test/api (muted from production routing; isolated GPU pool).
- Attachments: MAP workbook has checklist + signoffs; we also included a short runbook for the load ramp.

Preliminary results (staging runs; 2026-06-14 to 2026-06-15):
- Model: rw-infer/gptx-small-13b (8-bit quant) on A100-equivalent instance.
- Test harness: k6-based distributed runner, synthetic prompt set derived from your samples.
- Summary numbers (median of 3 runs):
  - P50 latency (request complete): 108 ms
  - P95 latency: 332 ms
  - TTFT (time to first token): 78 ms
  - Sustained throughput: 420 requests/sec (at concurrency = 8, avg output length = 72 tokens)
  - Tokens/sec: ~2,900 tokens/sec aggregate
  - Error rate: 0.6% (transient 429 spikes at concurrency = 16 during one run)

Interpretation: baseline meets your acceptance targets at concurrency 8 with comfortable headroom on P95. We did observe backpressure at 16 concurrent streams — we recommend using connection pooling + smaller batching windows for client-side calls if you plan to spike concurrency.

Next steps / asks for DataWave engineers:
1) Confirm two 2-hour load windows where your infra team can run the evaluation (we propose 2026-06-14 22:00–00:00 UTC and 2026-06-15 02:00–04:00 UTC).
2) Provide a list of 3 representative prompt templates (or confirm we can use the 200-sample set in the MAP workbook).
3) A single point of contact for on-call during the runs (Slack & escalation number).

I attached the MAP and will loop Laura with the consolidated results on 2026-06-17.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: DataWave_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook, checklist, runbook)

Subject: Re: MAP + perf eval: need test access and a results summary for exec review

Hi all —

I consolidated the full perf report after the DataWave-led runs on 2026-06-14 and 2026-06-15. Attached: rw-perf-summary-20260615.pdf (executive summary + raw CSVs). Key findings below:

Detailed summary (consolidated runs):
- Run configuration: 3x 30-minute steady-state windows per test day, clients from 2 geographic origins (us-west & us-east).
- P50 latency: 110 ms (stdev 12 ms)
- P95 latency: 340 ms (stdev 40 ms)
- TTFT median: 85 ms
- Sustained throughput (recommended config): 380–440 req/s at concurrency = 8 depending on avg output length
- Peak tested concurrency: 16 — observed intermittent 429s and slowdowns; at 16 concurrency throughput drops ~18% vs. 8 conc.
- CPU/GPU utilization: GPU steady 62–78% during steady-state; CPU spike during tokenization peaks.
- Suggestions: enable client-side request backoff with jitter, and use Redwood prefix cache for repeated prompts (saw 2.1x latency improvement on cached prefixes).

Executive recommendation:
- Proceed with the proposed MAP and target close by 2026-06-30. Pricing implications: sustained reservations for dedicated pool recommended if you expect sustained >300 req/s to reduce per-token cost.

I'll be available in the working session on 2026-06-17 to walk through the PDF.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Product Lead, Redwood Console

Attachment: rw-perf-summary-20260615.pdf
